title: Pick a ripe strawberry off a potted plant without bruising it or tearing its stalk, and put it in a basket
instruction: Pick the strawberry and put it in the basket.
context: Picking strawberries is familiar from gardens and pick-your-own farms, and the hard part is physical. A berry pulled straight along its stalk needs 13.94 N to come off, but bent against it only 3.17 N (Dimeas et al. 2013); pulled straight, the stalk can also break midway and leave a piece that punctures other berries (Yamamoto et al. 2014). Gripped harder than about 10 N it bruises: a light grip slips, a hard one bruises, so the berry must be tilted before it is pulled.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the table top. Pot: a black plastic 6 in azalea pot (15.2 cm across the top, 11.4 cm at the bottom, 11.4 cm tall, soil 0.4 cm below the rim), centred at (38.0, -10.0), set on marks on the table. Plant: a day-neutral strawberry plant (e.g. 'Albion') with no ripe fruit; its leaves, flowers and any green fruit on the far half of the pot. Truss: one of the plant's own fruit trusses (about 2 mm thick, about 14 cm long from the crown, sinking about 1 cm under a clipped berry), prepared once: flowers and fruit cut off, tip cut about 3 cm beyond the rim; it rises from the crown among the leaf stalks to about 15 cm high and arches towards the robot over the near rim on the pot's centre line (y -10.0), about 1 cm above the rim (a line on the rim marks the pot's turn). Berry: a fresh store-bought long-stem strawberry (sold for chocolate dipping), fully red, 14-16 g, about 2.8 cm across and 3.6 cm long, its stalk trimmed to 3.5 cm and joined end to end with the truss tip in a 2.5 mm silicone grafting clip, so it hangs tip down on 3 cm of its own stalk with its centre at (26.5, -10.0), 5.9 cm high (tip 4.1 cm), 3.5 cm beyond the rim. Basket: a square green molded-fiber quart berry basket (Pactiv 1 qt: 14.0 cm square at the top, 10.8 cm at the bottom, 8.3 cm tall), empty, centred at (23.0, -25.0). The left arm has nothing to do.
scoring: Tools: the trial video, a close-up photo of the berry taken right after the trial, and a ruler. Squeezed: at any moment a robot finger pressed the berry with more than 10 N (in simulation, the contact force; on real trials, a dented, flattened or leaking patch 3 mm or more across where a finger pressed); the trial then scores 0. Off: the berry no longer hangs from the plant. Torn: a piece of stalk more than 10 mm long remains above its calyx, wherever the stalk parted (in simulation, it came off with the pull within 45 degrees of its axis). In the basket: its centre inside the basket's walls and the berry resting on the basket's floor, any way up. Released: no part of the robot touches it. At the end: 0 if squeezed or still on the plant; 0.5 if off but not in the basket (held, on the table or on the floor), or if off and torn wherever it lies; 0.75 if off, not torn and in the basket but still touched; 1.0 if off, not torn, in the basket and released, held for 1 s. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: One berry per trial; plant, truss, pot and basket are reused. Berries: long-stem, any variety, fully red with no white or green shoulders, firm, unbruised, green calyx, 14-16 g (kitchen scale), at most 3.0 cm across, stalk at least 4 cm; stored unwashed and dry in their clamshell at 0-2 °C (UC Davis Postharvest; UC ANR), used within 5 days (Driscoll's). Trials at room temperature (20-25 °C): a session's berries come out of the refrigerator 2 h before its first trial so their flesh is at room temperature (bruising depends on flesh temperature, Ferreira et al. 2009); berries are handled only by the stalk. Per trial (a couple of minutes): pull the old stalk from the clip, trim a new berry's stalk to 3.5 cm and clip it to the truss tip, set the pot on its marks, check the tip height (4.1 cm) and overhang (3.5 cm) with a ruler, empty the basket. Wipe and dry the gripper pads after a berry leaks.
fidelity: Berry: the YCB strawberry scan, 15 g, convex-hull collider, pad friction 0.5. Truss and stalk: 17 bending 1 cm links from the crown that droop under the berry. The berry hangs on a stiff spring and comes off when the pull reaches 13.94/(1+3.40 sin a) N, a being the pull's angle to its axis: the measured 13.94 N straight and 3.17 N tilted, with a smooth curve between. Torn below 45 degrees is a modelling choice. Leaves don't collide; pot and basket are fixed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps; the right arm moved about between the pot and the basket and never grasped the berry); demo: 1.0
